title: Algebraicity of flat coherent families on a general separated finitely presented space
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention], and use algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] and their sheaf fibre products [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. Use quasi-coherent modules on small etale ringed sites and tensor pullback [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module, def-trf-space-etale-module-functors]. A module is finitely presented if etale locally it is the cokernel of a map between finite rank free modules. Relative flatness means flatness of stalks on etale scheme charts over the local rings of the base [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over]. A finite type module is etale locally finitely generated; support proper over the base means there are a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow X$ with $Z$ proper over the base and a finite type quasi-coherent module $N$ on $Z$ with $i_*N\simeq M$, as in [def-sfb-space-proper-quot-functor]. Let $f:X\to B$ be a separated morphism of finite presentation of algebraic spaces over $S$; morphism properties use [def-sfb-space-morphism-properties], and finite presentation includes quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness. Let $\mathcal C_{X/B}(T)$ have objects $(b:T\to B,M)$, where $M$ is a finitely presented quasi-coherent module on $X_T=X\times_BT$, flat over $T$ with support proper over $T$. Arrows over $v:T\to T_1$ are pullback isomorphisms $v_X^*M_1\simeq M$ with $b=b_1v$. These categories form an algebraic stack over $S$ [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack], using the fibred groupoid conventions of [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. If $B$ is a scheme, its structural morphism $\mathcal C_{X/B}\to B$ is locally of finite presentation: a smooth surjective scheme atlas has locally finitely presented composite to $B$ [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. No flatness of $f$ or Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

source.place: Tags 08KB (situation-coherent), 09DS (theorem-coherent-algebraic-general); for the scheme-base local-finite-presentation clause, 08KD (lemma-coherent-limits), together with the limit criterion in lem-sfb-stack-limit-preserving-lfp.

proof.text: Write $\mathcal C=\mathcal C_{X/B}$. By [lem-sfb-space-coherent-fppf-stack] it is an fppf stack, hence an etale stack. By [lem-sfb-space-coherent-diagonal] its isomorphism presheaves are algebraic spaces, so it has the required representable diagonal. All these statements require only finite presentation of $f$. Thus the remaining algebraicity assertion is the existence of a smooth surjective scheme atlas.

We first treat $B=\operatorname{Spec}\Lambda$ for a finitely generated $\mathbf Z$-algebra $\Lambda$, and regard the same groupoid as a groupoid on all schemes over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-coherent-limit-preserving] with $S=\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: $B\to S$ is locally finitely presented by [pqf-lem-lft-fp-locnoeth]; the base $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ is Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian]. The pushout equivalence [lem-sfb-space-coherent-pushout] supplies both (RS*) for square-zero ring fibre products and the Artinian nilpotent pushouts required by the Artin criterion. By [lem-sfb-space-coherent-tangent-finite] its tangent and infinitesimal automorphism spaces are finite dimensional for every finite type field over $\mathbf Z$. By [lem-sfb-space-coherent-formal-effectivity], every compatible complete-local adic system is effective; separatedness is used here. These are the limit, infinitesimal, tangent and formal hypotheses of [lem-sfb-artin-representable-diagonal-criterion].

source.place: Tag 09DS, reduction to finite type integer algebra and verification of axioms [1]--[4].

proof.text: For openness of versality retain this affine $B$. Take a compatible sequence $(b_n,M_n)$ over rings $R_n$ with surjective square-zero transition kernels, and put $R=\varprojlim R_n$. Since $B$ is affine, the compatible ring maps $\Lambda\to R_n$ define the ring map $\lambda\mapsto(b_n^\sharp(\lambda))_n$ into $R$, hence $b:\operatorname{Spec}R\to B$. The space $X_R\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is separated and finitely presented by [lem-sfb-space-separated-fp-composition, lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Apply [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-support-inverse-effectivity] to this space and the given $M_n$. Square-zero ideals are locally nilpotent, so it gives $M$ with all compatible reduction isomorphisms. Thus $(b,M)$ makes the original system effective. Together with the representable diagonal, (RS*) and continuity already obtained, [lem-sfb-artin-square-zero-effectivity-openness] gives openness of versality over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. No flatness of $X_R$ was used.

source.place: Tag 09DS, last paragraph; Tag 0CXB and Tag 0CXU.

proof.text: All hypotheses of [lem-sfb-artin-representable-diagonal-criterion] now hold over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Its size hypothesis follows from [def-weil-size-convention]: finite type fields have a set of representatives in the fixed small skeleton; finite presentations on a fixed set of etale charts, their gluing maps, and module isomorphisms form sets in the larger universe. Taking the union over that set of fields gives a common cardinal bound; the affine polynomial scheme in a set of variables of that cardinality bounds it. Apply the criterion to obtain an algebraic stack over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$. Its map remembering $b$ is a map to $B$. The equivalence of [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers] therefore regards it as an algebraic stack over $B$.

source.place: Tag 09DS, omitted set-theoretic axiom [-1] and application of Artin criterion; Tag 04X5.

proof.text: For any map $B'\to B$, the groupoid for $X_{B'}/B'$ is naturally the 2-fibre product $\mathcal C_{X/B}\times_{h_B}h_{B'}$: an object is $(b,M,b',b=b'\text{ followed by }B'\to B)$, so forgetting the redundant $b$ identifies it with $(b',M)$, and the same identity identifies arrows. This identification is compatible with every pullback. For an arbitrary affine $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$, take the directed set of finitely generated integer subalgebras $R_i\subset R$. It is nonempty, two stages are contained in the algebra generated by their union, and every element of $R$ is in a stage. These inclusions exhibit $R$ as their colimit by [lem-weil-pbc-directed-subalgebra-ring-colimit]. By [lem-sfb-fp-space-limit-category], $X$ descends to a finitely presented $X_i/R_i$. Increase $i$ using [lem-sfb-space-descend-separated] so $X_i/R_i$ is separated. Step 4 gives algebraicity of its family stack. Its 2-base change to $B$ is algebraic by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-fibre-products, lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers], and the explicit equivalence just given identifies it with $\mathcal C_{X/B}$.

source.place: Tag 08LP (remark-coherent-base-change); Tag 09DS, affine Noetherian approximation paragraph.

proof.text: For the atlas unions used next, let $W_a\to\mathcal F$ be representable smooth maps of schemes to a stack with representable diagonal. Form $W=\coprod_aW_a$ using [lem-weil-pbc-scheme-coproduct-family]; its clopen pieces glue their objects to an object over $W$ by stack descent. For any scheme $T\to\mathcal F$, its pullback is $\coprod_a(W_a\times_{\mathcal F}T)$: a map into $W$ is exactly a clopen partition with one map into each $W_a$, and the object isomorphisms restrict and glue on that partition. Each summand is an algebraic space. The coproduct is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-algebraic-space-coproduct], using etale scheme charts in the fixed universe. Its map to $T$ is smooth: choose the coproduct of smooth scheme charts of the summands, and use [lem-sfb-scheme-etale-source-target-properties] to test smoothness on this disjoint open cover and on further etale charts. Surjectivity is precisely joint field-extension local lifting for the summands. Thus a jointly surjective family yields a smooth surjective scheme atlas. This is a direct use of coproduct, stack descent and the cited chart locality statements; no algebraicity of $\mathcal F$ is used.

source.place: Tag 09DS, affine-cover atlas assembly, with coproduct chart tests spelled out.

proof.text: For a scheme $B$, choose an affine open cover $B=\bigcup B_a$. Step 5 gives smooth surjective scheme atlases $W_a\to\mathcal C_{X_{B_a}/B_a}$. Regard each atlas over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ by [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers]. The equivalence in step 5 identifies its target with the pullback of $B_a\to B$, so its composite to the total $\mathcal C_{X/B}$ is representable and smooth by [lem-sfb-fibred-groupoid-representable-smooth-calculus]. The atlas assembly in the preceding step makes $\coprod_aW_a\to\mathcal C_{X/B}$ representable, smooth and surjective. Together with the stack and diagonal from step 1 this is exactly the algebraic-stack definition [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]; [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers] then regards it over $B$. For the original algebraic-space $B$, choose a surjective etale scheme atlas $B'\to B$. By step 5 the pullback groupoid is $\mathcal C_{X_{B'}/B'}$, which is algebraic by the scheme case; its projection to $\mathcal C_{X/B}$ is representable etale surjective by the same calculus lemma. Composing a smooth surjective scheme atlas of this pullback with that projection again gives a representable smooth surjective scheme atlas. The same algebraic-stack definition gives algebraicity over the original $S$; regarding the intermediate scheme-base atlas over $S$ uses the equivalence with the common stack over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ in [lem-sfb-algebraic-stack-change-base-to-integers].

source.place: Tag 09DS, etale cover and affine open cover reductions, reversed to assemble the atlases.

proof.text: Finally let $B$ be a scheme. Apply [lem-sfb-space-coherent-limit-preserving] with base scheme $S=B$ and base space $B$ with its identity morphism, which is locally finitely presented. Thus for every directed affine inverse system over $B$, objects and isomorphisms descend, with eventual equality. We have already proved that $\mathcal C_{X/B}$ is an algebraic stack over $B$. The reverse implication of [lem-sfb-stack-limit-preserving-lfp] therefore says that $\mathcal C_{X/B}\to B$ is locally of finite presentation in precisely the smooth-atlas convention of the statement.
